notes: Prague's is Letiště Václava Havla. To the airport = na letiště; at the airport = na letišti.

examples.tl: Na letiště jede trolejbus 59 od metra Nádraží Veleslavín.
examples.en: Trolleybus 59 goes to the airport from Nádraží Veleslavín metro station.

notes: Never changes in the singular: na nádraží = to or at the station. Praha hlavní nádraží is written 'hl. n.'

examples.en: The train leaves from the main station.

notes: By train = vlakem. České dráhy (ČD) is the state railway; RegioJet and Leo Express are private rivals.

examples.en: I'm going to Brno by train.

notes: Prague has three lines: A (green), B (yellow), C (red). By metro = metrem.

examples.tl: Na Hrad jeďte metrem A na Malostranskou.
examples.en: For the Castle take metro line A to Malostranská.

notes: Feminine: ta tramvaj. By tram = tramvají. In Brno people call it 'šalina'.

examples.tl: Tramvaj číslo 22 jede na Pražský hrad.
examples.en: Tram number 22 goes to Prague Castle.

notes: By bus = autobusem. Long-distance coaches (RegioJet, FlixBus) mostly leave Prague from ÚAN Florenc.

examples.tl: Do Českého Krumlova jede autobus tři hodiny.
examples.en: The bus to Český Krumlov takes three hours.

notes: Never changes its ending. Order one in an app (Bolt, Uber, Liftago) rather than hailing one in the tourist center.

examples.en: We'll take a taxi to the airport.

notes: For transport only. In Prague buy it in the PID Lítačka app, at a yellow machine, or by card on board a tram.

examples.en: One 30-minute ticket, please.

notes: Everyday word for any ticket (train, cinema, concert). 1 lístek, 2 lístky, 5 lístků.

examples.en: Two tickets to Karlštejn, please.

notes: Prague tickets go by time: 30 minutes, 90 minutes, 24 hours, 72 hours. One ticket covers metro, trams and buses.

examples.en: A 24-hour ticket, please.

notes: For trams and buses; a metro or train stop is a 'stanice'. At the stop = na zastávce.

examples.en: Get off at the next stop.

notes: Metro and smaller rail stations. Stanice metra = metro station.

examples.en: At which station should I get off?

notes: Stations give both platform and track: 'třetí nástupiště, kolej pátá' = platform 3, track 5. Check the track number.

examples.tl: Vlak do Brna odjíždí z páté koleje.
examples.en: The train to Brno leaves from track five.

notes: Přestupuju = I'm changing. On the metro, signs saying 'Přestup' lead to the other line.

examples.en: You have to change at Můstek.

notes: Opposite: nastoupit = to get on. Vystupuju = I'm getting off.

examples.en: Where should I get off?

notes: Any trip on wheels: jedu = I'm going, jede = it goes, jedeme = we're going. On foot the verb is jít.

examples.en: Does this train go to Brno?

notes: Paper tickets must be stamped in the yellow box on trams and buses or at the metro entrance. Unstamped = a fine.

examples.en: Don't forget to validate your ticket.

notes: Plain clothes; shows a badge and says 'Kontrola jízdenek'. No valid ticket costs about 1 000 Kč on the spot.

examples.en: The inspector wanted to see my ticket.

notes: PID Lítačka is Prague's ticket app and travel card (PID = Prague Integrated Transport). Activate the ticket before boarding.

examples.tl: Jízdenku si koupím v aplikaci Lítačka.
examples.en: I'll buy the ticket in the Lítačka app.

notes: On boards as 'zpoždění 10 min'. Vlak má zpoždění = the train is delayed.

examples.en: How late is that train?

notes: Station boards: Odjezdy = departures, Příjezdy = arrivals. Airports use odlety and přílety.

examples.tl: Odjezd je v 9:42 z prvního nástupiště.
examples.en: Departure is at 9:42 from platform one.

notes: Of trains and buses; a plane's arrival is přílet.

examples.en: Arrival in Brno is at 11:30.

notes: Compulsory on RegioJet and SC Pendolino trains; optional but wise on busy ČD trains on Friday and Sunday.

examples.en: Do I need a seat reservation for this train?

notes: zpáteční jízdenka = return ticket; jednosměrná = one-way.

examples.tl: Zpáteční jízdenku do Kutné Hory, prosím.
examples.en: A return ticket to Kutná Hora, please.

notes: Literally 'only there'. The ticket clerk's question is 'Zpáteční?' (return?).

examples.en: – Return? – No, one way.

notes: A numbered tram or bus route, or a metro line (also called 'trasa').

examples.en: Which line goes to Florenc?

notes: Platform signs name the last stop: 'směr Háje' = toward Háje. Check it before you board.

examples.en: Take metro line C toward Háje.

notes: Announcement: 'Konečná stanice, prosíme, vystupte' = last stop, please get off. Declines like an adjective.

examples.en: Get off at the very last stop.

notes: In full: cestovní pas. Hotels have to see it at check-in.

examples.en: Here is my passport.

notes: Letadlo = plane, letenka = plane ticket.

examples.en: My flight is delayed.

notes: Board codes: Os = slow local train, R = rychlík, Ex / IC / EC = faster expresses, SC = Pendolino, RJ = Railjet.

examples.tl: Rychlík do Olomouce jede každou hodinu.
examples.en: The express to Olomouc runs every hour.

notes: jedna jízdenka becomes jednu jízdenku as the thing you ask for; do + genitive: Brno → do Brna, Praha → do Prahy.

examples.en: One ticket to Prague, please.

tl: V kolik jede vlak do Českého Krumlova?
en: What time is the train to Český Krumlov?
accept: When does the train to Český Krumlov leave?
What time is the train to Cesky Krumlov?
notes: do + genitive: Český Krumlov → do Českého Krumlova. From Prague you usually change in České Budějovice.

examples.tl: – V kolik jede vlak do Českého Krumlova? – V osm, s přestupem v Českých Budějovicích.
examples.en: – What time is the train to Český Krumlov? – At eight, with a change in České Budějovice.

notes: Platforms are posted only 10–20 minutes before departure: watch the board.

examples.tl: Z kterého nástupiště jede vlak do Plzně?
examples.en: Which platform does the train to Plzeň leave from?

en: Does this go to the airport?
notes: Ask the driver or anyone at the stop. Swap the end: na hlavní nádraží, do centra.

examples.tl: Promiňte, jede to na hlavní nádraží?
examples.en: Excuse me, does this go to the main station?

en: Where do I have to change?
accept: Where do I need to change?

examples.en: – Where do I have to change? – At Florenc.

notes: On ČD trains a paper or display above the seat shows whether it is reserved.

examples.tl: – Je tohle místo volné? – Ano, prosím.
examples.en: – Is this seat free? – Yes, go ahead.

notes: Heard in every metro car: 'Příští stanice: Můstek.' Trams and buses say 'Příští zastávka'.

examples.tl: Příští stanice: Muzeum, přestup na linku C.
examples.en: Next station: Muzeum, change for line C.

notes: The end of the famous Prague metro announcement. You only need to recognize it.

examples.tl: Ukončete, prosím, výstup a nástup, dveře se zavírají.
examples.en: Please finish exiting and boarding, the doors are closing.

en: Where can I buy a ticket?

examples.tl: – Kde si můžu koupit jízdenku? – V automatu nebo v aplikaci.
examples.en: – Where can I buy a ticket? – From the machine or in the app.

notes: Destination + prosím is all a taxi driver needs: Na hlavní nádraží, prosím.

examples.tl: Dobrý den, na hlavní nádraží, prosím.
examples.en: Hello, to the main station, please.

notes: Ask before you get into a street taxi; apps show the price up front.

examples.tl: Kolik to bude stát do centra?
examples.en: How much will it cost to the center?
Stop here at the corner, please.

notes: Said to whoever is blocking the door on a full tram or metro. If you aren't, step aside.

examples.en: – Excuse me, are you getting off? – Yes, me too.

notes: Jedu = I'm going by vehicle. do + genitive for towns: do Prahy, do Brna, do Plzně, do Olomouce.

examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to Prague.

tl: Platí tahle jízdenka i na tramvaj?
en: Is this ticket valid on the tram too?
accept: Is this ticket also valid for the tram?
notes: Platí = is valid (also 'he pays'). In Prague one ticket covers every mode within its time limit.

examples.tl: – Platí tahle jízdenka i na tramvaj? – Ano, na všechno.
examples.en: – Is this ticket valid on the tram too? – Yes, on everything.
